ch32.sub: The Religion about Jesus and the Religion of Jesus
ch32.sum: Christianity was born of the life and teachings of Jesus, yet after Pentecost the gospel of the kingdom was changed into a gospel about the risen Christ. Peter founded the church, Paul shaped its theology, the Greek world received and Hellenized it, and the Roman world paganized and institutionalized it. In the process many of Jesus' ideals were compromised, but they were not lost, and Christianity became one of the greatest powers for good on earth. This chapter traces the formation and transformation of Christianity, its contributions and its handicaps, and arrives at the conclusion that what the world now most needs is, once again, the living Jesus himself. A religion about Jesus may be preached, but the religion of Jesus must be lived.
ch32.s1: From the Gospel of the Kingdom to the Gospel about Christ
ch32.s1.u1.k: After Pentecost the message of Jesus became the gospel of the Lord Jesus Christ.
ch32.s1.u1.p: What Jesus entrusted to his apostles was the gospel of the fatherhood of God and the brotherhood of man. But the minds of the disciples who had experienced the resurrection were filled with Jesus himself, and the center of their proclamation shifted to his life, death, and resurrection and to the hope of his speedy return. The brotherly love of the early communities was truly wonderful, yet it sprang from fellowship among believers in Jesus more than from the recognition that all men are brothers. The shift was a mistake, and at the same time the beginning of the greatest religion mankind had yet known.

text: The gospel of the kingdom, the message of Jesus, had been suddenly changed into the gospel of the Lord Jesus Christ. They now proclaimed the facts of his life, death, and resurrection and preached the hope of his speedy return to this world to finish the work he began.

True, a marvelous manifestation of brotherly love and unexampled good will did spring up in these early communities of believers. But it was a fellowship of believers in Jesus, not a fellowship of brothers in the family kingdom of the Father in heaven. … They made the great mistake of using the living and illustrative commentary on the gospel of the kingdom for that gospel, but even that represented the greatest religion mankind had ever known.

ch32.s1.u2.k: Peter founded the church, and Paul transformed the new gospel into Christianity.
ch32.s1.u2.p: The formation of Christianity bears clear names. In the enthusiasm of Pentecost Peter inaugurated the religion of the risen and glorified Christ, and Paul systematized it through his experience on the Damascus road and his own theology, carrying it to the gentile world. Thus the gospel of the kingdom is rooted in the religious experience of the Jesus of Galilee, while Christianity rests chiefly on the religious experience of Paul.

text: Peter was the real founder of the Christian church; Paul carried the Christian message to the gentiles, and the Greek believers carried it to the whole Roman Empire.

In the enthusiasm of Pentecost, Peter unintentionally inaugurated a new religion, the religion of the risen and glorified Christ. The Apostle Paul later on transformed this new gospel into Christianity, a religion embodying his own theologic views and portraying his own personal experience with the Jesus of the Damascus road. The gospel of the kingdom is founded on the personal religious experience of the Jesus of Galilee; Christianity is founded almost exclusively on the personal religious experience of the Apostle Paul.

ch32.s1.u3.k: As Christianity became Occidentalized, it began to lose its universal appeal to all races.
ch32.s1.u3.p: Christianity grew on the foundation of Jewish theology, absorbing Zoroastrian teachings and Greek philosophy along the way. In the process it became so thoroughly Occidentalized that to non-European peoples it looked like a strange revelation of a strange God. Christianity glorified Jesus as the Christ but largely forgot his personal gospel, the fatherhood of God and the brotherhood of all men.

text: The Christian religion is the religion about the life and teachings of Christ based upon the theology of Judaism, modified further through the assimilation of certain Zoroastrian teachings and Greek philosophy, and formulated primarily by three individuals: Philo, Peter, and Paul. It has passed through many phases of evolution since the time of Paul and has become so thoroughly Occidentalized that many non-European peoples very naturally look upon Christianity as a strange revelation of a strange God and for strangers.

As the original teachings of Jesus penetrated the Occident, they became Occidentalized, and as they became Occidentalized, they began to lose their potentially universal appeal to all races and kinds of men. … It has glorified Jesus as the Christ, the Messianic anointed one from God, but has largely forgotten the Master's personal gospel: the Fatherhood of God and the universal brotherhood of all men.

ch32.s2.u1.k: The Western world had a great culture but hungered for a soul-satisfying religion.
ch32.s2.u1.p: Christianity spread swiftly through the Roman world because of that world's spiritual void. People who had inherited great achievements in philosophy, art, and politics had grown skeptical of every existing religion and philosophy, and the popularity of the mystery cults revealed a deep longing for survival and personal righteousness. The mysteries could not satisfy that longing, but they prepared the way for the reception of Jesus, who brought the bread and the water of life.

text: Western civilization was at this time intellectual, war weary, and thoroughly skeptical of all existing religions and universe philosophies. The peoples of the Western world, the beneficiaries of Greek culture, had a revered tradition of a great past. They could contemplate the inheritance of great accomplishments in philosophy, art, literature, and political progress. But with all these achievements they had no soul-satisfying religion. Their spiritual longings remained unsatisfied.

The popularity of the mysteries reveals man's quest for survival, thus portraying a real hunger and thirst for personal religion and individual righteousness. Although the mysteries failed adequately to satisfy this longing, they did prepare the way for the subsequent appearance of Jesus, who truly brought to this world the bread of life and the water thereof.

ch32.s2.u2.k: Greek philosophy and the teachings of Jesus shared the goal of the emergence of the individual.
ch32.s2.u2.p: The Hellenization of Christianity was not merely a corruption. The Greek taught intellectual liberty and Jesus taught spiritual liberty, and the meeting of the two became a new charter for human freedom. Then Rome, which had an empire but no God, and the Christians, who had a God but no empire, embraced each other. Rome gave the Western world a unity of political rule, Greece a unity of culture, and Christianity a unity of religious thought.

text: And there was something strangely alike in Greek philosophy and many of the teachings of Jesus. They had a common goal—both aimed at the emergence of the individual. … The Greek taught intellectual liberalism leading to political freedom; Jesus taught spiritual liberalism leading to religious liberty. These two ideas put together constituted a new and mighty charter for human freedom; they presaged man's social, political, and spiritual liberty.

After the consolidation of Roman political rule and after the dissemination of Christianity, the Christians found themselves with one God, a great religious concept, but without empire. The Greco-Romans found themselves with a great empire but without a God to serve as the suitable religious concept for empire worship and spiritual unification. The Christians accepted the empire; the empire adopted Christianity. The Roman provided a unity of political rule; the Greek, a unity of culture and learning; Christianity, a unity of religious thought and practice.

ch32.s2.u3.k: The early leaders compromised Jesus' ideals, yet those ideals remain latent in his gospel.
ch32.s2.u3.p: Compromise with the pagan world brought ritual and pageantry into Christianity. Yet what was gained in exchange was great: a higher standard of human morals, an enlarged concept of God, the hope of immortality as part of a recognized religion, and above all, Jesus of Nazareth given to hungry souls. The compromised ideals were not discarded; they only slumber, and one day they will assert their full power upon the world.

text: Wisely or unwisely, these early leaders of Christianity deliberately compromised the ideals of Jesus in an effort to save and further many of his ideas. And they were eminently successful. But mistake not! these compromised ideals of the Master are still latent in his gospel, and they will eventually assert their full power upon the world.
By this paganization of Christianity the old order won many minor victories of a ritualistic nature, but the Christians gained the ascendancy in that:
1. A new and enormously higher note in human morals was struck.
2. A new and greatly enlarged concept of God was given to the world.
3. The hope of immortality became a part of the assurance of a recognized religion.
4. Jesus of Nazareth was given to man's hungry soul.

ch32.s3.u1.k: Christianity is an extemporized religion, yet it holds enough of Jesus' teachings to be immortal.
ch32.s3.u1.p: It is easy to point out the defects of Christianity, but the text first asks that it not be lightly regarded. Christianity is the product of the moral genius of God-knowing men of many races across many ages. The teachings set in motion by the ordinary disciples of a crucified carpenter conquered the Roman world and later awoke of themselves from a thousand-year coma. The source of that vitality is the teaching of Jesus still contained within it.

text: But the Christianity of even the twentieth century must not be despised. It is the product of the combined moral genius of the God-knowing men of many races during many ages, and it has truly been one of the greatest powers for good on earth, and therefore no man should lightly regard it, notwithstanding its inherent and acquired defects.

But Christianity is a mighty religion, seeing that the commonplace disciples of a crucified carpenter set in motion those teachings which conquered the Roman world in three hundred years and then went on to triumph over the barbarians who overthrew Rome. … And then, when this Christian religion became comatose for more than a thousand years as a result of an overdose of mysteries and paganism, it resurrected itself and virtually reconquered the whole Western world. Christianity contains enough of Jesus' teachings to immortalize it.

ch32.s3.u2.k: Christianity is handicapped by its identification with the social system of Western civilization.
ch32.s3.u2.p: The greatest difficulty Christianity faces comes not from external enemies but from alliances of its own making. The world sees Christianity as part of the industrial life and moral standards of the West, the apparent sponsor of a society that tolerated science without idealism and power without conscience. The church's entanglement in commerce and politics, and its smothering of newborn faith and persecution of truth bearers in unorthodox dress, are remembered as a betrayal of the Master.

text: Christianity suffers under a great handicap because it has become identified in the minds of all the world as a part of the social system, the industrial life, and the moral standards of Western civilization; and thus has Christianity unwittingly seemed to sponsor a society which staggers under the guilt of tolerating science without idealism, politics without principles, wealth without work, pleasure without restraint, knowledge without character, power without conscience, and industry without morality.

But there is no excuse for the involvement of the church in commerce and politics; such unholy alliances are a flagrant betrayal of the Master. And the genuine lovers of truth will be slow to forget that this powerful institutionalized church has often dared to smother newborn faith and persecute truth bearers who chanced to appear in unorthodox raiment.

ch32.s3.u3.k: The turbulent history of Christianity shows that it possesses deep powers of recovery.
ch32.s3.u3.p: Hellenization, paganization, secularization, institutionalization, decadence and hibernation, threatened extinction, then rejuvenation and fragmentation: the record of Christianity reads like a catalog of decline, yet the text reads in that very record an inherent vitality. Now Christianity faces a greater test, an age ruled by scientific minds and materialistic tendencies. But the text affirms that in the struggle between the secular and the spiritual, the religion of Jesus will eventually triumph.

text: Christianity exhibits a history of having originated out of the unintended transformation of the religion of Jesus into a religion about Jesus. It further presents the history of having experienced Hellenization, paganization, secularization, institutionalization, intellectual deterioration, spiritual decadence, moral hibernation, threatened extinction, later rejuvenation, fragmentation, and more recent relative rehabilitation. Such a pedigree is indicative of inherent vitality and the possession of vast recuperative resources.

Religion is now confronted by the challenge of a new age of scientific minds and materialistic tendencies. In this gigantic struggle between the secular and the spiritual, the religion of Jesus will eventually triumph.

ch32.s4.u1.k: The true church is an invisible spiritual brotherhood, marked by unity rather than uniformity.
ch32.s4.u1.p: Jesus did not found the so-called Christian church, but he has fostered it as the best existing exponent of his work on earth. The true church, however, is not a visible organization but the invisible brotherhood of those joined by faith to the living Jesus. The hope of unity for a divided Christendom lies not in doctrinal uniformity but in the living Jesus. Social organizations may serve that brotherhood, but they must never replace it.

text: Jesus did not found the so-called Christian church, but he has, in every manner consistent with his nature, fostered it as the best existent exponent of his lifework on earth.

The living Jesus is the only hope of a possible unification of Christianity. The true church—the Jesus brotherhood—is invisible, spiritual, and is characterized by unity, not necessarily by uniformity. … And this brotherhood is destined to become a living organism in contrast to an institutionalized social organization. It may well utilize such social organizations, but it must not be supplanted by them.

ch32.s4.u2.k: Christianity has served the world greatly, but what is now most needed is Jesus.
ch32.s4.u2.p: The renewal of Christianity does not lie in a return to the primitive church; one must go forward from where one stands. What the world needs to see is Jesus living again in the lives of spirit-born men and women. The hope of Christianity is to cease sponsoring Western civilization, to bow humbly before the cross it has so valiantly extolled, and there to learn anew the living gospel of the fatherhood of God and the brotherhood of man.

text: Christianity has indeed done a great service for this world, but what is now most needed is Jesus. The world needs to see Jesus living again on earth in the experience of spirit-born mortals who effectively reveal the Master to all men. It is futile to talk about a revival of primitive Christianity; you must go forward from where you find yourselves.

The hope of modern Christianity is that it should cease to sponsor the social systems and industrial policies of Western civilization while it humbly bows itself before the cross it so valiantly extols, there to learn anew from Jesus of Nazareth the greatest truths mortal man can ever hear—the living gospel of the fatherhood of God and the brotherhood of man.

ch32.s4.u3.k: The world needs not secondhand religion but firsthand religion.
ch32.s4.u3.p: Beyond the limitation of being a religion about Jesus, Christianity bears another: most people hold their faith secondhand, just as it was handed down by their teachers. As words describing a beautiful thing cannot thrill like the sight of it, so creeds cannot take the place of the experience of knowing God's presence.

text: The world needs more firsthand religion. Even Christianity—the best of the religions of the twentieth century—is not only a religion about Jesus, but it is so largely one which men experience secondhand. They take their religion wholly as handed down by their accepted religious teachers. … Descriptive words of things beautiful cannot thrill like the sight thereof, neither can creedal words inspire men's souls like the experience of knowing the presence of God.

ch32.qs1: Is my faith closer to a religion about Jesus or to the religion of Jesus?
ch32.qs2: What attitude in my life would it mean to see the defects of the church without lightly regarding it?
ch32.qs3: What can I do to turn a faith handed down to me into a faith I experience firsthand?
ch33.sub: The Living Experience of Knowing God
ch33.sum: Religion, as The Urantia Book presents it, is neither a system of doctrine nor a mystic ecstasy. It is the living experience of a person who knows God as Father and man as brother. The divine spirit meets man less in feeling than in his highest thinking, and that meeting becomes spiritual insight. Religious experience cannot be bestowed or borrowed; it grows in proportion to the quest for final values, and its driving power is a living faith that governs the way one lives. This chapter considers in turn the nature of religious experience, its growth, the character of faith, and the fruits the experience bears in service and in peace. The reality of religion shows itself more in living than in explanation, and one who has found God lives as if already in the presence of the Eternal.
ch33.s1.u1.k: True religion is to know God as Father and man as brother.
ch33.s1.u1.p: The definition of religion is simple: the personal experience of knowing God as Father, and the realization that naturally follows from it, knowing man as brother. The first is wholly inward, but the second requires a social adjustment of the self to other selves. Religion therefore begins within and moves outward. A belief that leans on threats of punishment or promises of mystical reward is far from this definition.

text: While religion is exclusively a personal spiritual experience—knowing God as a Father—the corollary of this experience—knowing man as a brother—entails the adjustment of the self to other selves, and that involves the social or group aspect of religious life. Religion is first an inner or personal adjustment, and then it becomes a matter of social service or group adjustment.
Always keep in mind: True religion is to know God as your Father and man as your brother. Religion is not a slavish belief in threats of punishment or magical promises of future mystical rewards.

ch33.s1.u2.k: Religion is not the product of reason, yet viewed from within it is altogether reasonable.
ch33.s1.u2.p: Religion rejects two opposite misunderstandings. One sees it as a philosophic system to be reasoned out and proved by evidence; the other sees it as an indescribable ecstasy enjoyed only by a few mystics. Religion is not the product of reason, yet viewed from within it is altogether reasonable; it is not intellectual assent to doctrine but insight into reality.

text: True religion is not a system of philosophic belief which can be reasoned out and substantiated by natural proofs, neither is it a fantastic and mystic experience of indescribable feelings of ecstasy which can be enjoyed only by the romantic devotees of mysticism. Religion is not the product of reason, but viewed from within, it is altogether reasonable.

True religion is an insight into reality, the faith-child of the moral consciousness, and not a mere intellectual assent to any body of dogmatic doctrines. True religion consists in the experience that "the Spirit itself bears witness with our spirit that we are the children of God." Religion consists not in theologic propositions but in spiritual insight and the sublimity of the soul's trust.

ch33.s1.u3.k: It is our thoughts, not our feelings, that lead us Godward.
ch33.s1.u3.p: Contrary to the common view that religion belongs to the realm of emotion, the text says that the divine spirit contacts man in his highest and most spiritualized thinking. This does not belittle feeling. It means that the eye which discerns God is the eye of the mind, and that mind must be pure.

text: The divine spirit makes contact with mortal man, not by feelings or emotions, but in the realm of the highest and most spiritualized thinking. It is your thoughts, not your feelings, that lead you Godward. The divine nature may be perceived only with the eyes of the mind. But the mind that really discerns God, hears the indwelling Adjuster, is the pure mind.

ch33.s2.u1.k: Religion cannot be bestowed or borrowed; it grows as the quest for final values grows.
ch33.s2.u1.p: Religion is not a possession that can be inherited or passed on by instruction. Like all growth of body, mind, and spirit, religious growth happens unconsciously, and no one can force it. But one can supply favorable conditions. Man's only contribution to growth is the mobilization of all the powers of his personality, which is living faith.

text: Religion cannot be bestowed, received, loaned, learned, or lost. It is a personal experience which grows proportionally to the growing quest for final values. … But nobility itself is always an unconscious growth.

Man cannot cause growth, but he can supply favorable conditions. Growth is always unconscious, be it physical, intellectual, or spiritual. … Man's sole contribution to growth is the mobilization of the total powers of his personality—living faith.

ch33.s2.u2.k: Spiritual growth moves from awakening to needs, to discerning meanings, to discovering values.
ch33.s2.u2.p: Spiritual growth has an order. First one awakens to what is lacking, then discerns the meanings of things, and at last discovers what is truly valuable. The evidence of such growth is not the amount of theological knowledge but motives born of love, unselfish ministry, and wholehearted worship of the ideals of divinity. Spirituality thus becomes the measure both of one's nearness to God and of one's usefulness to others.

text: Spiritual growth is first an awakening to needs, next a discernment of meanings, and then a discovery of values. The evidence of true spiritual development consists in the exhibition of a human personality motivated by love, activated by unselfish ministry, and dominated by the wholehearted worship of the perfection ideals of divinity.

Spirituality becomes at once the indicator of one's nearness to God and the measure of one's usefulness to fellow beings. Spirituality enhances the ability to discover beauty in things, recognize truth in meanings, and discover goodness in values.

ch33.s2.u3.k: Emotion alone is false conversion, and mystic states must not be confused with spiritual communion.
ch33.s2.u3.p: Dramatic conversion experiences and mystic ecstasies are easily taken for the summit of religion. The text calmly observes that the very factors which induce such states reveal their danger. States produced by fatigue, fasting, fear, and violent emotion can be dangerous. Feeling must be joined by faith. Jesus' communion with his Adjuster was something quite different from such mystic states.

text: But emotion alone is a false conversion; one must have faith as well as feeling. To the extent that such psychic mobilization is partial, and in so far as such human-loyalty motivation is incomplete, to that extent will the experience of conversion be a blended intellectual, emotional, and spiritual reality.

The direct communion with one's Thought Adjuster, such as occurred in the later years of Jesus' life in the flesh, should not be confused with these so-called mystical experiences. The factors which contribute to the initiation of mystic communion are indicative of the danger of such psychic states. The mystic status is favored by such things as: physical fatigue, fasting, psychic dissociation, profound aesthetic experiences, vivid sex impulses, fear, anxiety, rage, and wild dancing.

ch33.s3.u1.p: To accept a teaching as true is still only belief. It becomes faith when it moves life and actually governs the way one lives. Beliefs can be held in common by a group, but faith grows only in the heart of the individual. And faith honors truth, beauty, and goodness without worshiping them; it turns to God alone, who personifies them all.

text: Belief has attained the level of faith when it motivates life and shapes the mode of living. The acceptance of a teaching as true is not faith; that is mere belief. … One believes truth, admires beauty, and reverences goodness, but does not worship them; such an attitude of saving faith is centered on God alone, who is all of these personified and infinitely more.

Belief is always limiting and binding; faith is expanding and releasing. Belief fixates, faith liberates. … Beliefs may become group possessions, but faith must be personal. Theologic beliefs can be suggested to a group, but faith can rise up only in the heart of the individual religionist.

ch33.s3.u2.k: Genuine spiritual faith is proved by the way it responds amid trial and adversity.
ch33.s3.u2.p: The reality of faith shows itself less on calm days than on hard ones. The text lists the responses of a soul that possesses faith: it advances morality against animal tendencies, trusts the goodness of God in bitter disappointment, finds courage in the face of calamity, and keeps its poise amid illness and pain. These responses, arising where life looks like defeat, reveal the potential divinity of the emerging soul.

text: Through religious faith the soul of man reveals itself and demonstrates the potential divinity of its emerging nature by the characteristic manner in which it induces the mortal personality to react to certain trying intellectual and testing social situations. Genuine spiritual faith (true moral consciousness) is revealed in that it:
1. Causes ethics and morals to progress despite inherent and adverse animalistic tendencies.
2. Produces a sublime trust in the goodness of God even in the face of bitter disappointment and crushing defeat.
3. Generates profound courage and confidence despite natural adversity and physical calamity.
4. Exhibits inexplicable poise and sustaining tranquillity notwithstanding baffling diseases and even acute physical suffering.

ch33.s3.u3.k: Religionists live as if already in the presence of the Eternal.
ch33.s3.u3.p: The elements of religious experience are hard to analyze, but its results are not hard to observe. Believers live today as if immortality were already in their grasp. Religion does not remove human troubles, but it dissolves, illuminates, and transcends them. And faith bridges the gulf between the intellect's logic, which knows the First Cause as It, and the soul's affirmation that the First Cause is He, the heavenly Father.

text: It is difficult to identify and analyze the factors of a religious experience, but it is not difficult to observe that such religious practitioners live and carry on as if already in the presence of the Eternal. Believers react to this temporal life as if immortality already were within their grasp.

Religion does not remove or destroy human troubles, but it does dissolve, absorb, illuminate, and transcend them. … Religious faith—the positive leading of the indwelling divine presence—unfailingly enables the God-knowing man to bridge that gulf existing between the intellectual logic which recognizes the Universal First Cause as It and those positive affirmations of the soul which aver this First Cause is He, the heavenly Father of Jesus' gospel, the personal God of human salvation.

ch33.s4.u1.k: Religion is not a technique for peace of mind but an impulse that organizes the soul for service.
ch33.s4.u1.p: To treat religion only as a private refuge is to miss its essence. True religion enlists the whole self in the loyal service of loving God and serving man. It takes nothing away from life but adds new meaning to everything and generates fresh enthusiasm and courage. Yet unless that zeal is governed by spiritual insight and faithfulness to ordinary social duties, it can turn into a dangerous crusading spirit.

text: Religion is not a technique for attaining a static and blissful peace of mind; it is an impulse for organizing the soul for dynamic service. It is the enlistment of the totality of selfhood in the loyal service of loving God and serving man.

Genuine religion takes nothing away from human existence, but it does add new meanings to all of life; it generates new types of enthusiasm, zeal, and courage. It may even engender the spirit of the crusader, which is more than dangerous if not controlled by spiritual insight and loyal devotion to the commonplace social obligations of human loyalties.

ch33.s4.u2.k: One who finds God is impelled into loving service to refresh his fellows.
ch33.s4.u2.p: Religious desire is hunger for divine reality, and religious experience is the consciousness of having found God. One who has found God does not seek to boast of it. He simply seeks loving contact with others so that the goodness welling up in his soul may overflow to refresh them. This unselfish interest in others arises because the same God fragment indwells every person. Philosophic uniformity is beyond reach, yet spiritual unity is possible.

text: Religious desire is the hunger quest for divine reality. Religious experience is the realization of the consciousness of having found God. And when a human being does find God, there is experienced within the soul of that being such an indescribable restlessness of triumph in discovery that he is impelled to seek loving service-contact with his less illuminated fellows, not to disclose that he has found God, but rather to allow the overflow of the welling-up of eternal goodness within his own soul to refresh and ennoble his fellows.

The unity of religious experience among a social or racial group derives from the identical nature of the God fragment indwelling the individual. It is this divine in man that gives origin to his unselfish interest in the welfare of other men. … A group of mortals can experience spiritual unity, but they can never attain philosophic uniformity.

ch33.s4.u3.k: A remarkable mark of religious living is a dynamic peace that passes all understanding.
ch33.s4.u3.p: The peace religion gives is not a motionless calm. It is a cosmic poise maintained in the midst of service and adventure, a stability that settles where doubt and turmoil have gone. This peace is immune to disappointment. One who has grasped the reality of the Supreme and pursues the goal of the Ultimate enjoys both the glory of triumph and a deep sense of security.

text: One of the most amazing earmarks of religious living is that dynamic and sublime peace, that peace which passes all human understanding, that cosmic poise which betokens the absence of all doubt and turmoil. Such levels of spiritual stability are immune to disappointment.

There is a sense of security, associated with the realization of triumphing glory, resident in the consciousness of the religionist who has grasped the reality of the Supreme, and who pursues the goal of the Ultimate.

ch33.qs1: Does my faith remain a belief handed down to me, or is it a faith that actually changes the way I live?
ch33.qs2: When I suffer disappointment or injustice, how does my faith show itself in my response?
ch33.qs3: If the experience of knowing God has ever led me into service to others, what did that look like?
ch34.sub: Two Ways of Communion with the Father
ch34.sum: Prayer and worship are two ways in which man communes personally with God. Prayer is not magic that tries to fit God to man's wishes but a process of fitting the human will to the divine will, and God answers prayer by giving a larger grasp of truth, beauty, and goodness. The prayer of one wholly dedicated to doing the Father's will cannot remain unanswered. Worship goes a step further: it asks nothing and is offered to God simply for what he is, in self-forgetting adoration. This chapter considers the nature and conditions of prayer, the character of worship, and the way in which prayer grows into worship. Prayer enriches the life, while worship illuminates destiny and makes us ever more like the One we worship.
ch34.s1.u1.k: Prayer is the sincere and longing look of the child to its spirit Father.
ch34.s1.u1.p: Jesus taught prayer not as a set formula but as an attitude of the soul. Prayer is the soul's spontaneous expression toward the spirit, the fellowship between a son and his Father. It is the sincere attitude of reaching heavenward for the attainment of one's ideals, a psychological process of exchanging the human will for the divine will. Prayer thus has its place within God's plan for turning what is into what ought to be.

text: Prayer is entirely a personal and spontaneous expression of the attitude of the soul toward the spirit; prayer should be the communion of sonship and the expression of fellowship. … True praying is the sincere attitude of reaching heavenward for the attainment of your ideals.

Prayer is the sincere and longing look of the child to its spirit Father; it is a psychologic process of exchanging the human will for the divine will. Prayer is a part of the divine plan for making over that which is into that which ought to be.

ch34.s1.u2.k: Magic tries to adjust Deity to conditions; prayer adjusts the personality to the will of Deity.
ch34.s1.u2.p: Prayer and magic may look alike, but they point in opposite directions. Magic seeks to move supernatural power to obtain a desired result; prayer seeks to bring oneself into line with the will of God. So prayer does not change God, but it changes the one who prays. In those who have prayed with faith and confident expectation there have grown peace of mind, cheerfulness, courage, self-mastery, and fair-mindedness.

text: Magic was an attempt to adjust Deity to conditions; prayer is the effort to adjust the personality to the will of Deity. True prayer is both moral and religious; magic is neither.

Remember, even if prayer does not change God, it very often effects great and lasting changes in the one who prays in faith and confident expectation. Prayer has been the ancestor of much peace of mind, cheerfulness, calmness, courage, self-mastery, and fair-mindedness in the men and women of the evolving races.

ch34.s1.u3.k: Prayer is not an escape from conflict but a stimulus to growth in the face of conflict.
ch34.s1.u3.p: Prayer does not replace action. A prayer that hands over to God the problem one ought to solve oneself can become a form of sloth. But a prayer asking for wisdom and strength to light and sustain one's way while wrestling with the problem is always right. So the text counsels us to pray for values rather than things, for growth rather than gratification. Prayer is not a way around difficulty but a way of growing through it.

text: Do not be so slothful as to ask God to solve your difficulties, but never hesitate to ask him for wisdom and spiritual strength to guide and sustain you while you yourself resolutely and courageously attack the problems at hand.
Prayer is not a technique of escape from conflict but rather a stimulus to growth in the very face of conflict. Pray only for values, not things; for growth, not for gratification.

ch34.s2.u1.k: God answers prayer with an enlarged grasp of truth, beauty, and goodness.
ch34.s2.u1.p: The answer to prayer is not the same as receiving exactly what one asked for. As a wise parent does not grant a foolish request but gives the child what is truly needed, so the heavenly Father gives the spirit and many more blessings to those who ask. God's answer comes as a larger revelation of truth, a deeper appreciation of beauty, and a higher concept of goodness. That is why prayer is the most potent stimulus to spiritual growth.

text: God answers man's prayer by giving him an increased revelation of truth, an enhanced appreciation of beauty, and an augmented concept of goodness. Prayer is a subjective gesture, but it contacts with mighty objective realities on the spiritual levels of human experience; it is a meaningful reach by the human for superhuman values. It is the most potent spiritual-growth stimulus.

Which of you who is a father, if his son asks unwisely, would hesitate to give in accordance with parental wisdom rather than in the terms of the son's faulty petition? … If you, then, being mortal and finite, know how to answer prayer and give good and appropriate gifts to your children, how much more shall your heavenly Father give the spirit and many additional blessings to those who ask him?

ch34.s2.u2.k: The prayer of one wholly dedicated to doing the Father's will cannot remain unanswered.
ch34.s2.u2.p: There is only one way for every prayer to be answered: that what we ask be wholly in accord with the Father's will. When what the true son desires and what the infinite Father wills become the same, it already is. The five conditions of effective prayer that Jesus taught, unselfishness, faith, sincerity, intelligence, and trust in the Father's all-wise will, all point toward this harmony.

text: When you have become wholly dedicated to the doing of the will of the Father in heaven, the answer to all your petitions will be forthcoming because your prayers will be in full accordance with the Father's will, and the Father's will is ever manifest throughout his vast universe. What the true son desires and the infinite Father wills IS. Such a prayer cannot remain unanswered, and no other sort of petition can possibly be fully answered.
Jesus taught that effective prayer must be:
1. Unselfish—not alone for oneself.
2. Believing—according to faith.
3. Sincere—honest of heart.
4. Intelligent—according to light.
5. Trustful—in submission to the Father's all-wise will.

ch34.s2.u3.k: Be fair in prayer; do not expect God to love you more than his other children.
ch34.s2.u3.p: Prayer calls for fairness. A prayer that asks God for favoritism, to love me more than my friends, neighbors, or enemies, is not ethical. Prayer becomes more ethical when it seeks forgiveness and wisdom for self-control. Moreover, deliberately harboring iniquity in the heart gradually cuts off personal communion with God.

text: In all your praying be fair; do not expect God to show partiality, to love you more than his other children, your friends, neighbors, even enemies. … Prayer is somewhat more ethical when it deals with forgiveness and seeks wisdom for enhanced self-control.

Naturally God hears the petition of his child, but when the human heart deliberately and persistently harbors the concepts of iniquity, there gradually ensues the loss of personal communion between the earth child and his heavenly Father.

ch34.s2.u4.k: Prayer begins with material petition and grows into prayer for one's fellows.
ch34.s2.u4.p: The prayers of childhood, whether of an individual or a race, are selfish and material. Even such prayers have value insofar as they call forth effort, so the mature should be careful not to discourage the prayers of the immature. Yet prayer must grow. Jesus' praying was a remedy for harmful introspection, and he usually prayed in the plural, for his fellows rather than for himself.

text: The childhood of an individual or a race is characterized by primitive, selfish, and materialistic praying. And, to a certain extent, all such petitions are efficacious in that they unvaryingly lead to those efforts and exertions which are contributory to achieving the answers to such prayers. … But the spiritually advanced person should exercise great caution in attempting to discourage the primitive or immature mind regarding such prayers.

Prayer is an antidote for harmful introspection. At least, prayer as the Master taught it is such a beneficent ministry to the soul. Jesus consistently employed the beneficial influence of praying for one's fellows. The Master usually prayed in the plural, not in the singular. Only in the great crises of his earth life did Jesus ever pray for himself.

ch34.s3.u1.k: Worship is for its own sake; it asks nothing and expects nothing.
ch34.s3.u1.p: The great difference between prayer and worship lies in the presence or absence of self-interest. Prayer contains an element of asking, but true worship contains none. True worship asks nothing for the worshiper and expects nothing in return. Worship is the spontaneous answer of the heart before One who is loved.

text: Worship is for its own sake; prayer embodies a self- or creature-interest element; that is the great difference between worship and prayer. … Worship asks nothing and expects nothing for the worshiper.

ch34.s3.u2.k: Prayer is self-reminding thought; worship is self-forgetting thought.
ch34.s3.u2.p: In prayer a person is still conscious of himself and his needs; in worship he forgets himself. Worship is therefore effortless attention, a restful form of spiritual exertion. In worship the part identifies with the whole, the finite with the Infinite, the son with the Father, time with eternity. Worship is the son's personal communion with the Father, and it refreshes the soul and makes it creative.

text: Prayer is self-reminding—sublime thinking; worship is self-forgetting—superthinking. Worship is effortless attention, true and ideal soul rest, a form of restful spiritual exertion.

Worship is the act of a part identifying itself with the Whole; the finite with the Infinite; the son with the Father; time in the act of striking step with eternity. Worship is the act of the son's personal communion with the divine Father, the assumption of refreshing, creative, fraternal, and romantic attitudes by the human soul-spirit.

ch34.s3.u3.k: The worship experience is the Adjuster's attempt to convey the soul's unutterable longings to the Father.
ch34.s3.u3.p: Worship is not something a person does alone. The indwelling Adjuster seeks to convey to the Father the soul's inexpressible longings, and that soul is the joint creation of the human mind and the Adjuster. That is why a mind of material limitations cannot be fully conscious of the deep meaning of worship. How far one realizes the reality of the worship experience depends not on intellectual level but on the growth of the evolving immortal soul.

text: The worship experience consists in the sublime attempt of the betrothed Adjuster to communicate to the divine Father the inexpressible longings and the unutterable aspirations of the human soul—the conjoint creation of the God-seeking mortal mind and the God-revealing immortal Adjuster.

The mind of material limitations can never become highly conscious of the real significance of true worship. Man's realization of the reality of the worship experience is chiefly determined by the developmental status of his evolving immortal soul.

ch34.s4.u1.k: Prayer may enrich the life, but worship illuminates destiny.
ch34.s4.u1.p: The text observes that modern religions have overemphasized prayer and neglected the more essential communion of worship. Prayer is not to be abandoned; it is a stairway into worship. Prayer led Jesus' soul into deep communion with the Supreme Rulers of the universe, and it will lead mortals into the communion of true worship. How much of heaven's blessing a person receives depends on the soul's spiritual capacity for receptivity.

text: Prayer is indeed a part of religious experience, but it has been wrongly emphasized by modern religions, much to the neglect of the more essential communion of worship. The reflective powers of the mind are deepened and broadened by worship. Prayer may enrich the life, but worship illuminates destiny.

Prayer led Jesus up to the supercommunion of his soul with the Supreme Rulers of the universe of universes. Prayer will lead the mortals of earth up to the communion of true worship. The soul's spiritual capacity for receptivity determines the quantity of heavenly blessings which can be personally appropriated and consciously realized as an answer to prayer.

ch34.s4.u2.k: Worship makes us increasingly like the One worshiped; it looks to the One to serve the many.
ch34.s4.u2.p: The indwelling spirit speaks best when the human mind is in an attitude of true worship. Worship is a transforming experience that makes us more and more like the One we worship, the way by which the finite gradually approaches the presence of the Infinite. Yet worship is not an escape from the world. We look to the One in order to be inspired to serve the many.

text: The spirit of the Father speaks best to man when the human mind is in an attitude of true worship. … Worship, taught Jesus, makes one increasingly like the being who is worshiped. Worship is a transforming experience whereby the finite gradually approaches and ultimately attains the presence of the Infinite.

Worship is the technique of looking to the One for the inspiration of service to the many. Worship is the yardstick which measures the extent of the soul's detachment from the material universe and its simultaneous and secure attachment to the spiritual realities of all creation.

ch34.qs1: Is my praying closer to fitting God to my will, or to fitting my will to God's?
ch34.qs2: Have I experienced worship that asks nothing and is offered to God simply for who he is?
ch34.qs3: How can I make room in my daily life for a time of silent waiting after prayer?
ch35.sum: If the descending Sons come down from above to serve, the ascending sons start from below and climb toward God. Their largest host is the mortals of animal origin, but guardian seraphim, Material Sons, and midwayers also walk this path. Mortals are the last link in the chain of beings called sons of God; they are now faith sons, and they become ascending sons at the moment of fusion with spirit. This chapter considers the classes of ascending sons, the sonship of mortals, the seven stages from planet to Paradise, and the destinies that differ according to the type of fusion, affirming that all these destinies rest under the same love of the Father. Even the faintest desire to find God is enough for any soul to set out on this path.
ch35.s1.u1.k: The story of the ascending sons is a record of divine love and gracious condescension.
ch35.s1.u1.p: The Urantia Book divides beings broadly into descending sons and ascending sons. The ascending sons are revealed in seven classes: Father-fused, Son-fused, and Spirit-fused mortals, evolutionary seraphim, ascending Material Sons, translated midwayers, and Personalized Adjusters. This list is no mere table of categories. The very fact that beings of the lowliest animal origin can rise testifies to the love the Deities pour out without stint on all the universes of time and space.

text: AS IN many of the major groups of universe beings, seven general classes of the Ascending Sons of God have been revealed:
1. Father-fused Mortals.
2. Son-fused Mortals.
3. Spirit-fused Mortals.
4. Evolutionary Seraphim.
5. Ascending Material Sons.
6. Translated Midwayers.
7. Personalized Adjusters.

The story of these beings, from the lowly animal-origin mortals of the evolutionary worlds to the Personalized Adjusters of the Universal Father, presents a glorious recital of the unstinted bestowal of divine love and gracious condescension throughout all time and in all universes of the far-flung creation of the Paradise Deities.

ch35.s1.u2.k: Not mortals only, but angels and midwayers also share the opportunity of Paradise ascent.
ch35.s1.u2.p: The path of ascent is not open to humans alone. Guardian seraphim attain ascendant sonship through experience and service with ascending mortals, and many join the Mortal Corps of the Finality. Midwayers too, though their Paradise ascent is long deferred, are released from planetary duty once their world reaches the era of light and life. Ascent is a road walked together by very different beings, and service is the key that opens it.

text: Mortal creatures of animal origin are not the only beings privileged to enjoy sonship; the angelic hosts also share the supernal opportunity to attain Paradise. Guardian seraphim, through experience and service with the ascending mortals of time, also achieve the status of ascendant sonship. Such angels attain Paradise through Seraphington, and many are even mustered into the Corps of Mortal Finality.

Although deprived of the immediate benefits of the planetary bestowals of the descending Sons of God, though the Paradise ascent is long deferred, nevertheless, soon after an evolutionary planet has attained the intermediate epochs of light and life (if not before), both groups of midway creatures are released from planetary duty.

ch35.s2.u1.k: Mortals are the last link in the chain of sons, and the Father draws nearest through the indwelling Adjuster.
ch35.s2.u1.p: The personal touch of the Eternal Son passes down through a series of sons, decreasingly divine and increasingly human, until it reaches a being that man can see and touch. At the end of that chain stand mortals. God the Father does not appear in direct personal form to his countless creatures, but that does not make him distant. The One who is farthest from us in personality draws nearest to us in the indwelling Thought Adjuster, communing with the very soul.

text: Mortals represent the last link in the chain of those beings who are called sons of God. The personal touch of the Original and Eternal Son passes on down through a series of decreasingly divine and increasingly human personalizations until there arrives a being much like yourselves, one you can see, hear, and touch.

Although God the Father cannot be with you by direct personality manifestation, he is in you and of you in the identity of the indwelling Thought Adjusters, the divine Monitors. Thus does the Father, who is the farthest from you in personality and in spirit, draw the nearest to you in the personality circuit and in the spirit touch of inner communion with the very souls of his mortal sons and daughters.

ch35.s2.u2.k: Mortals are not yet of the divine order, yet they are even now faith sons of God.
ch35.s2.u2.p: Mortals are not yet divine by nature; they become ascending sons only upon fusion with an eternal spirit. Yet even before that, man is already a son. The Father has given him personality together with a measure of the divine spontaneity of freewill that God shares with his sons, and a fragment of the Father himself indwells him. Man is therefore even now directly related to the divine Father of all the Sons of God.

text: You mortals are divinely beloved, and every one of you may choose to accept the certain destiny of a glorious experience, but you are not yet by nature of the divine order; you are wholly mortal. You will be reckoned as ascending sons the instant fusion takes place, but the status of the mortals of time and space is that of faith sons prior to the event of the final amalgamation of the surviving mortal soul with some type of eternal and immortal spirit.

4. Of his divine free-willness, the Universal Father has given you your creature personalities. You have been endowed with a measure of that divine spontaneity of freewill action which God shares with all who may become his sons.
5. There dwells within you a fragment of the Universal Father, and you are thus directly related to the divine Father of all the Sons of God.

ch35.s2.u3.k: Every soul with even the faintest desire to find God will survive.
ch35.s2.u3.p: The secret of survival lies in identification with spirit. Yet the text sets the threshold of survival remarkably low. All that is needed is a willingness to co-operate with the Adjuster and a desire to find God and attain perfection, even if that desire is only the first faint flicker of a primitive grasp of the true light. Survival is not a reward for knowledge or achievement; it depends on the direction of the will toward God.

text: Spirit identification constitutes the secret of personal survival and determines the destiny of spiritual ascension. And since the Thought Adjusters are the only spirits of fusion potential to be identified with man during the life in the flesh, the mortals of time and space are primarily classified in accordance with their relation to these divine gifts, the indwelling Mystery Monitors.

As to the chances of mortal survival, let it be made forever clear: All souls of every possible phase of mortal existence will survive provided they manifest willingness to co-operate with their indwelling Adjusters and exhibit a desire to find God and to attain divine perfection, even though these desires be but the first faint flickers of the primitive comprehension of that "true light which lights every man who comes into the world."

ch35.s3: The Seven Stages of the Ascending Career
ch35.s3.u1.k: Ascending pilgrims pass through seven stages, from planetary mortals to Paradise arrivals.
ch35.s3.u1.p: The universe career of a mortal is arranged in clear stages. One is born and lives on a planet, rests after death as a sleeping survivor, awakens and learns on the mansion worlds, rises as a morontia progressor, becomes a ward of the superuniverse, passes through Havona as a pilgrim, and arrives at Paradise. The starting point is the same for all: mortals of every world are evolutionary beings of animal origin, and after death they fraternize as one morontia family on the mansion worlds.

text: While the mortal survivors of time and space are denominated ascending pilgrims when accredited for the progressive ascent to Paradise, these evolutionary creatures occupy such an important place in these narratives that we here desire to present a synopsis of the following seven stages of the ascending universe career:
1. Planetary Mortals.
2. Sleeping Survivors.
3. Mansion World Students.
4. Morontia Progressors.
5. Superuniverse Wards.
6. Havona Pilgrims.
7. Paradise Arrivals.
Mortals are all animal-origin evolutionary beings of ascendant potential. … After natural death all types of ascenders fraternize as one morontia family on the mansion worlds.

ch35.s3.u2.k: In passing from morontia to spirit, mind, personality, and character remain unchanged.
ch35.s3.u2.p: Each stage of the ascent is a continuation, not a break. Morontia progressors rising from the mansion worlds to the local universe headquarters learn by serving on countless assignments with their teachers and senior brethren. Near the time they leave the local universe they acquire true spirit identity, yet this is only a slight transition. The form changes, but mind, personality, and character carry on unchanged. The ascender remains the same person to the end.

text: From the mansion worlds on up through the spheres of the system, constellation, and the universe, mortals are classed as morontia progressors; they are traversing the transition spheres of mortal ascension. As the ascending mortals progress from the lower to the higher of the morontia worlds, they serve on countless assignments in association with their teachers and in company with their more advanced and senior brethren.

Mortals acquire real spirit identity just before they leave the local universe headquarters for the receiving worlds of the minor sectors of the superuniverse. Passing from the final morontia stage to the first or lowest spirit status is but a slight transition. The mind, personality, and character are unchanged by such an advance; only does the form undergo modification.

ch35.s3.u3.k: To reside on Paradise means that one has found God.
ch35.s3.u3.p: The one who was a creature of flesh and blood on earth becomes a morontia being in the local universe, an evolving spirit in the superuniverse, and receives spiritual education in earnest in Havona. At last he stands on Paradise as a perfected spirit. To dwell there means that one has found God, and those fused with the Father are mustered into the Mortal Corps of the Finality. Yet this arrival is not an end but the beginning of new learning in divinity and absonity.

text: On earth you were a creature of flesh and blood; through the local universe you were a morontia being; through the superuniverse you were an evolving spirit; with your arrival on the receiving worlds of Havona your spiritual education begins in reality and in earnest; your eventual appearance on Paradise will be as a perfected spirit.

On reaching Paradise with residential status, you begin the progressive course in divinity and absonity. Your residence on Paradise signifies that you have found God, and that you are to be mustered into the Mortal Corps of the Finality. Of all the creatures of the grand universe, only those who are Father fused are mustered into the Mortal Corps of the Finality.

ch35.s4.u1.k: Because the Father has bestowed himself, he asks ultimate perfection of man.
ch35.s4.u1.p: The command to be perfect flows from the Father's gift. Because the Father has placed his own spirit within man, he can ask for the perfection of becoming one with that spirit. Adjuster-fused mortals are the only class of humans who all traverse the circuits of Havona and find God on Paradise, and before them the career of universal service lies wide open. The text declares that this dignity of destiny and glory of attainment await every one.

text: These are the mortals who have been commanded by the Universal Father, "Be you perfect, even as I am perfect." The Father has bestowed himself upon you, placed his own spirit within you; therefore does he demand ultimate perfection of you.

Fusion with a fragment of the Universal Father is equivalent to a divine validation of eventual Paradise attainment, and such Adjuster-fused mortals are the only class of human beings who all traverse the Havona circuits and find God on Paradise. To the Adjuster-fused mortal the career of universal service is wide open. What dignity of destiny and glory of attainment await every one of you!

ch35.s4.u2.k: Mortal destinies differ, but none is greater or lesser than another.
ch35.s4.u2.p: Destiny differs according to the type of fusion. Spirit-fused mortals generally remain in the local universe, Son-fused survivors in the superuniverse, while Adjuster-fused mortals go on to penetrate the universe of universes, because the fused spirit returns to its level of origin. But the text plainly says not to read these differences as a ranking. The destinies are simply different, and there is no favoritism or arbitrariness in the working of the survival plan.

text: Spirit-fused mortals are, generally speaking, confined to a local universe; Son-fused survivors are restricted to a superuniverse; Adjuster-fused mortals are destined to penetrate the universe of universes. The spirits of mortal fusion always ascend to the level of origin; such spirit entities unfailingly return to the sphere of primal source.

That mortal destinies do thus vary in no wise proves that one is necessarily greater or lesser than another, merely that they differ. … There is no favoritism, nothing arbitrary, in the selective operation of the divine plan of mortal survival.

ch35.s4.u3.k: Sonship is the supreme relationship of the creature to the Creator.
ch35.s4.u3.p: The story of the ascending sons returns in the end to the Father's love. The Father loves each son individually, personally, and irreplaceably, and that love eclipses every other fact, including the differences of destiny. So man can recognize his place in the family of divine sonship and begin to feel the obligation to take up every help the survival plan so freely offers, a plan illuminated by the life of a bestowal Son.

text: The Father loves each of his sons, and that affection is not less than true, holy, divine, unlimited, eternal, and unique—a love bestowed upon this son and upon that son, individually, personally, and exclusively. And such a love utterly eclipses all other facts. Sonship is the supreme relationship of the creature to the Creator.

As mortals you can now recognize your place in the family of divine sonship and begin to sense the obligation to avail yourselves of the advantages so freely provided in and by the Paradise plan for mortal survival, which plan has been so enhanced and illuminated by the life experience of a bestowal Son.

ch35.qs1: How does the fact that my starting point is lowly change my understanding of God's love?
ch35.qs2: How does the teaching that even a faint desire to find God suffices for survival change the way I see other people?
ch35.qs3: If my personality and character continue after death, what kind of character am I cultivating now?
ch36.sub: From the Mansion Worlds to the Threshold of Spirit
ch36.sum: Death is not an end but a door of transition. The survivor who has laid aside the flesh resumes life on the mansion worlds just where death overtook him, awakening as the same person with every worth-while memory. The morontia life is the transition career that lies between matter and spirit, a process of learning what was not learned on earth, correcting defects of character, and growing into universe-mindedness. The Gods do not transform man into a perfected spirit by a single act of magic; they lead him through many stages of gradual change. This chapter considers the continuity beyond death, the education of the mansion worlds, the divine method of gradual change, and the journey toward the threshold of spirit.
ch36.s1.u1.k: Death is a technique of escape from life in the flesh and the entrance to the morontia career.
ch36.s1.u1.p: The Urantia Book pictures death not as a dreadful severance but as a technique: a way of escape from the life of the material flesh, beyond which wait seven worlds of corrective training and cultural education. A survivor awakening on the mansion worlds may notice little difference except a different body. The tabernacle of flesh and blood has been left behind on the world of birth, but life itself goes on unbroken.

text: Mortal death is a technique of escape from the material life in the flesh; and the mansonia experience of progressive life through seven worlds of corrective training and cultural education represents the introduction of mortal survivors to the morontia career, the transition life which intervenes between the evolutionary material existence and the higher spirit attainment of the ascenders of time who are destined to achieve the portals of eternity.

When you go from Urantia to the first mansion world, you will notice considerable change, but if you had come from a more normal and progressive sphere of time, you would hardly notice the difference except for the fact that you were in possession of a different body; the tabernacle of flesh and blood has been left behind on the world of nativity.

ch36.s1.u2.k: The survivor begins over there right where he left off down here.
ch36.s1.u2.p: Between death and resurrection a person gains nothing but the fact of survival. Intellectual training and spiritual development resume at exactly the level where they were interrupted. Death, in other words, does not suddenly make anyone wise or holy. Yet the mansion worlds are also the place where, as a butterfly emerges from the caterpillar, the true personality once hidden in the material flesh is revealed for the first time.

text: On mansion world number one (or another in case of advanced status) you will resume your intellectual training and spiritual development at the exact level whereon they were interrupted by death. Between the time of planetary death or translation and resurrection on the mansion world, mortal man gains absolutely nothing aside from experiencing the fact of survival. You begin over there right where you leave off down here.

Just as a butterfly emerges from the caterpillar stage, so will the true personalities of human beings emerge on the mansion worlds, for the first time revealed apart from their onetime enshroudment in the material flesh.

ch36.s1.u3.k: Every memory of survival value is preserved by the Adjuster throughout the ascending career.
ch36.s1.u3.p: To the question whether the survivor is really the same person, the text answers with memory. Purely animal and material associations perish with the brain, but everything worth while and of survival value is counterparted and kept by the Adjuster. The persistence of memory is proof that the original self has been preserved. Thus what was worth while remains part of personal memory throughout the ascendant career.

text: Your Adjuster memory remains fully intact as you ascend the morontia life. Those mental associations that were purely animalistic and wholly material naturally perished with the physical brain, but everything in your mental life which was worth while, and which had survival value, was counterparted by the Adjuster and is retained as a part of personal memory all the way through the ascendant career.
The persistence of memory is proof of the retention of the identity of original selfhood; it is essential to complete self-consciousness of personality continuity and expansion.

ch36.s2: Correction and Education on the Mansion Worlds
ch36.s2.u1.k: Almost the entire experience of the first mansion world is deficiency ministry.
ch36.s2.u1.p: Before they are any paradise of reward, the mansion worlds are a school of healing and correction. Survivors from worlds like Urantia arrive with many defects of character and deficiencies of experience, so the chief activities of the first world are devoted to correcting these legacies of the life in the flesh. On the second world intellectual conflicts and mental disharmonies are healed. God's plan receives a person as he is and patiently raises him from there.

text: Almost the entire experience of mansion world number one pertains to deficiency ministry. Survivors arriving on this first of the detention spheres present so many and such varied defects of creature character and deficiencies of mortal experience that the major activities of the realm are occupied with the correction and cure of these manifold legacies of the life in the flesh on the material evolutionary worlds of time and space.
Mansonia number two more specifically provides for the removal of all phases of intellectual conflict and for the cure of all varieties of mental disharmony.

ch36.s2.u2.k: The destiny of eternity is determined moment by moment by the achievements of daily living.
ch36.s2.u2.p: The morontia instructor on the first mansion world uses brief statements of human philosophy to help new sojourners grasp the meaning of mota. Several of them remind us that there are no short cuts on the ascending path. The soul is made divine not by what it does but by what it strives to do, and death adds nothing to intellect or spiritual endowment. Since the acts of today are the destiny of tomorrow, postponement can never be avoidance.

text: 22. The evolving soul is not made divine by what it does, but by what it strives to do.
23. Death added nothing to the intellectual possession or to the spiritual endowment, but it did add to the experiential status the consciousness of survival.
24. The destiny of eternity is determined moment by moment by the achievements of the day by day living. The acts of today are the destiny of tomorrow.

ch36.s2.u3.k: A real birth of cosmic consciousness takes place on the fifth mansion world.
ch36.s2.u3.p: The education of the mansion worlds does not stop at correcting defects. On the fifth mansion world a real birth of cosmic consciousness takes place. Now study becomes voluntary rather than required, unselfish service becomes natural, and worship becomes spontaneous. When goodness once practiced with effort becomes second nature, a real morontia character is budding.

text: A real birth of cosmic consciousness takes place on mansonia number five. … Study is becoming voluntary, unselfish service natural, and worship spontaneous. A real morontia character is budding; a real morontia creature is evolving.

ch36.s2.u4.k: Ascenders learn to be faithful, earnest, and cheerful under pressure.
ch36.s2.u4.p: The path of ascent is an earnest struggle, but not a joyless one. The ministers of the mansion worlds teach how to let pressure produce stability, to accept challenges without complaint, and to face difficulties without fear. They ask: if you fail, will you rise to try again? And beings striving upward under sustained stress have the greatest need of humor and relaxation.

text: From them you will learn to let pressure develop stability and certainty; to be faithful and earnest and, withal, cheerful; to accept challenges without complaint and to face difficulties and uncertainties without fear. They will ask: If you fail, will you rise indomitably to try anew?

The need for the relaxation and diversion of humor is greatest in those orders of ascendant beings who are subjected to sustained stress in their upward struggles. The two extremes of life have little need for humorous diversions. Primitive men have no capacity therefor, and beings of Paradise perfection have no need thereof.

ch36.s3.u1.k: The Gods do not change a creature of animal nature into a perfected spirit by a single act of magic.
ch36.s3.u1.p: Many religious traditions imagine that a person becomes a perfected spirit at the moment of death. The text firmly calls such ideas pleasing fables. There can be no magic in the dissolution of the material body that instantly turns a human mind into an immortal spirit. When God wants perfect beings, he creates them so from the beginning. But he never undertakes to convert beings of animal origin into perfection in a single step.

text: THE Gods cannot—at least they do not—transform a creature of gross animal nature into a perfected spirit by some mysterious act of creative magic. When the Creators desire to produce perfect beings, they do so by direct and original creation, but they never undertake to convert animal-origin and material creatures into beings of perfection in a single step.

What magic could death, the natural dissolution of the material body, hold that such a simple step should instantly transform the mortal and material mind into an immortal and perfected spirit? Such beliefs are but ignorant superstitions and pleasing fables.

ch36.s3.u2.k: The morontia life begins already on earth, at the moment the soul is conceived.
ch36.s3.u2.p: The morontia life does not begin only after death. The soul is conceived at the moment the Adjuster indwells a mind capable of moral choice, and from then on the morontia career has already begun. In the days of the flesh the divine spirit dwells in man almost as a thing apart, but in the morontia life that spirit becomes a real part of the personality. Through hundreds of gradual transformations a person rises from matter to spirit.

text: You should understand that the morontia life of an ascending mortal is really initiated on the inhabited worlds at the conception of the soul, at that moment when the creature mind of moral status is indwelt by the spirit Adjuster.

In the days of the mortal flesh the divine spirit indwells you, almost as a thing apart—in reality an invasion of man by the bestowed spirit of the Universal Father. But in the morontia life the spirit will become a real part of your personality, and as you successively pass through the 570 progressive transformations, you ascend from the material to the spiritual estate of creature life.

ch36.s3.u3.k: Fusion with the Adjuster follows a final and irrevocable choice for the eternal career.
ch36.s3.u3.p: The most brilliant event of the morontia career is the fusion of the human mind with the divine Adjuster, usually achieved in fact on the fifth or sixth mansion world. Fusion occurs only when it has been pronounced that the human nature has made a final and irrevocable choice for the eternal career. God does not run ahead of human choice. He waits until free choice has matured and then brings about the eternal at-onement.

text: This is a brilliant age for ascending mortals and usually witnesses the perfect fusion of the human mind and the divine Adjuster. In potential, this fusion may have occurred previously, but the actual working identity many times is not achieved until the time of the sojourn on the fifth mansion world or even the sixth.
Fusion with the Adjuster never occurs until the mandates of the superuniverse have pronounced that the human nature has made a final and irrevocable choice for the eternal career.

ch36.s4.u1.k: On the seventh mansion world the differences of origin vanish, and the last remnants of the mark of the beast are removed.
ch36.s4.u1.p: On the seventh mansion world the differences between those from isolated and retarded worlds and those from advanced worlds are virtually erased. The remnants of unfortunate heredity, unwholesome environment, and unspiritual tendencies are all washed away. A disadvantaged starting point does not become an eternal handicap. And when the ascender leaves the system headquarters for Edentia, the personality begun in the flesh is at last fully unified and proclaimed a true child of the Most Highs.

text: Any discernible differences between those mortals hailing from the isolated and retarded worlds and those survivors from the more advanced and enlightened spheres are virtually obliterated during the sojourn on the seventh mansion world. Here you will be purged of all the remnants of unfortunate heredity, unwholesome environment, and unspiritual planetary tendencies. The last remnants of the "mark of the beast" are here eradicated.

The mortal personality initiated on the evolutionary worlds and tabernacled in the flesh—indwelt by the Mystery Monitors and invested by the Spirit of Truth—is not fully mobilized, realized, and unified until that day when such a Jerusem citizen is given clearance for Edentia and proclaimed a true member of the morontia corps of Nebadon—an immortal survivor of Adjuster association, a Paradise ascender, a personality of morontia status, and a true child of the Most Highs.

ch36.s4.u2.k: The goal of the survival plan is not endless ease but transcendent service.
ch36.s4.u2.p: The morontia career is the evolutionary portal to spirit life, leading on to the goal of time, the finding of God on Paradise. Yet the purpose of all this labor and training is not merely that man should survive to enjoy endless bliss. God's purpose in making the whole universe one vast training school is to prepare man for a transcendent service hidden beyond the horizon of the present universe age.

text: From the time of graduation from the mansion worlds to the attainment of spirit status in the superuniverse career, ascending mortals are denominated morontia progressors. Your passage through this wonderful borderland life will be an unforgettable experience, a charming memory. It is the evolutionary portal to spirit life and the eventual attainment of creature perfection by which ascenders achieve the goal of time—the finding of God on Paradise.

The mortal-survival plan has a practical and serviceable objective; you are not the recipients of all this divine labor and painstaking training only that you may survive just to enjoy endless bliss and eternal ease. There is a goal of transcendent service concealed beyond the horizon of the present universe age.

ch36.qs1: If after death I begin again right where I left off, where am I standing now?
ch36.qs2: How might I correct here and now habits such as procrastination and avoidance that must otherwise be rooted out on the mansion worlds?
ch36.qs3: How does knowing that gradual growth, not sudden change, is God's method help me view my own slow progress?
ch37.sub: The Paradise Destiny of Ascending Mortals
ch37.sum: Ascending mortals who reach Paradise and find God are mustered into the Corps of Mortal Finaliters. Around the core of Father-fused mortals the corps includes glorified seraphim, Havona natives, midwayers, Material Sons, and Gravity Messengers, all received as equals without losing their individuality. Yet arrival is not the end. The finaliters now return to serve in the universes of time, undergoing what may be called postgraduate training in universe administration. This chapter considers the composition of the corps, its present mission, the mobilization of the seven corps of finality, and what their unrevealed destiny in the universes of outer space may imply.
ch37.s1.u1.k: The Corps of Mortal Finaliters is the present known destination of Adjuster-fused mortals.
ch37.s1.u1.p: At the end of the long ascent, mortals arrive at the Corps of the Finality. The corps is made up of six groups: Havona natives, Gravity Messengers, glorified mortals, adopted seraphim, and glorified Material Sons and midway creatures. They now minister to the universes of space and administer worlds settled in light and life, but the text cautiously conjectures that their future destination is the universes of outer space now being organized.

text: THE Corps of Mortal Finaliters represents the present known destination of the ascending Adjuster-fused mortals of time. But there are other groups who are also assigned to this corps. The primary finaliter corps is composed of the following:
1. Havona Natives.
2. Gravity Messengers.
3. Glorified Mortals.
4. Adopted Seraphim.
5. Glorified Material Sons.
6. Glorified Midway Creatures.

While the Corps of the Mortal Finality is mobilizing on Paradise, and while they now so extensively minister to the universes of space and administer the worlds settled in light and life, their future destination must be the now-organizing universes of outer space. At least that is the conjecture of Uversa.

ch37.s1.u2.k: The finaliters embrace both the perfect and the perfected.
ch37.s1.u2.p: The beauty of this corps lies in the meeting of very different beings. Havona natives, perfect beings of direct creation, bring to the corps the viewpoint of one born in perfection. Many guardian seraphim who have watched over mortals ascend with their wards, take the finaliter oath, and forever accept the destiny of their mortal companions. Those perfect from the beginning and those perfected through experience form a single body.

text: These perfect beings of direct and divine creation are of great assistance to the Mortal Corps of Finality, and they will undoubtedly be of even greater service in the far-distant future. They provide the viewpoint of one born in perfection and divine repleteness. The finaliters thus embrace both phases of experiential existence—perfect and perfected.

Many of the faithful seraphic guardians of mortals are permitted to go through the ascendant career with their human wards, and many of these guardian angels, after becoming Father fused, join their subjects in taking the finaliter oath of eternity and forever accept the destiny of their mortal associates.

ch37.s1.u3.k: All finaliters are received as equals, yet that equality never erases individuality.
ch37.s1.u3.p: The corps is organized according to working associations on the worlds of space and the experience accumulated through the long ascendant career.
